message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate the submission against the rubric criteria.

C1: Mission concept and rationale (40% weight, levels 7-10 accomplished, 4-6 adequate, 0-3 deficient). The submission has a clear mission goal, objectives, requirements, users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM), rationale with references. Strong. Some issues: "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" — actually 30% increase in acidity (pH decrease), which is roughly correct phrasing but "30 percent more acidic" is a common simplification. Reference [6] is NOAA "How does climate change affect coral reefs" but cited for BoM combining images with SST products — that's a mismatch. Also [4] is a Nature news article, not the actual Asner paper. Minor. Overall accomplished, maybe 8-9. Let me say 9? The concept is clear, complete, well-referenced, users identified with needs mapped to objectives. I'd give 9.

C2: Project plan (30%). Gantt chart present, task descriptions, contingencies table, information sources table, rationale for ordering tied to mission. Very strong. Accomplished. Maybe 9. The plan fits within mission narrative — yes, explains why order follows mission. Contingencies robust. Information sources listed. 9.

C3: Preliminary progress (10%). Hand calcs for orbit: a, T, orbits/day, inclination, ground track shift, swath. Interpretation. STK scenario set up. Good preliminary results with interpretation. Accomplished, 8-9. Let me check technical correctness: a = 6978 km, T = 2π√(a³/μ). a³ = 6978³ = 3.398e11 km³. /398600 = 852,500 s². sqrt = 923.3 s. ×2π = 5801 s. Correct. Orbits/day 14.9 correct. Inclination 97.8° for 600 km sun-sync — reasonable (600 km SSO ~97.8°). Ground track shift: 360° × T/86164 = 360 × 5801/86164 = 24.24°. Correct. But "≈2,700 km" — 24.2° at equator = 24.2 × 111.3 = 2,694 km. Correct. Swath 10 m × 6000 pixels = 60 km. Correct.

Interpretation: "reef is up to about 250 km wide" — the GBR is up to ~250 km wide in places? Actually the GBR extends ~2300 km long and up to ~250 km wide in the southern part. Reasonable. "neighbouring ground tracks are 2,700 km apart on the same day" — correct for same-day adjacent tracks. Good.

One issue: the swath of 60 km with 10 m GSD and 6000 pixels — fine. But the conclusion that weekly coverage not guaranteed — reasonable.

C3 accomplished, 9.

C4: Report presentation (20%). Well-structured, clear headings, good writing, figures/tables labelled, references cited in text and match list. Check references: [1]-[11] all cited? [1] cited, [2] cited, [3] cited, [4] cited, [5] cited, [6] cited, [7] cited, [8] cited, [9] cited, [10] cited, [11] cited. Yes all cited. Reference [6] cited for BoM SST — mismatch but minor. Formatting consistent. Accomplished, 9.

Let me reconsider C1 mark. The rubric levels are 7-10 for accomplished. I'll give 9.

Actually, let me be careful about the "30 percent more acidic" — this is a factual simplification; ocean pH has dropped 0.1 units = ~30% increase in H+ concentration, so "30% more acidic" is defensible.

Reference [6] cited for "Bureau of Meteorology, which can combine the images with its sea surface temperature products [6]" — but [6] is NOAA climate change page, not BoM. Minor citation mismatch.

C1: 9.

Let me finalize marks: C1=9, C2=9, C3=9, C4=9.

Hmm, maybe differentiate a bit. C2 is very strong with contingencies and sources — 9. C3 strong — 9. C4 — 9.

Actually let me reconsider whether any should be lower. The report is quite polished. I'll keep 9s but maybe C1=9, C2=9, C3=8, C4=9. C3 preliminary progress is good but limited (only hand calcs, STK scenario just set up). Still accomplished. 8.

Let me set C3=8.

Requirements:
R1: met — mission concept benefits Australia, users, rationale.
R2: partial — relates plan to space segment (launch, orbit) but preliminary plan is more about schedule; the mission concept doesn't deeply apply course material on launch/orbits yet. Actually the plan mentions launch/orbit stages and hand calcs on orbit. I'd say partial — the plan references launch and orbit but doesn't yet apply detailed course material. Hmm. The requirement: "Relate the preliminary plan to the mission's space segment, applying relevant course material such as launch and orbits." The Gantt includes Launch Specifics, Orbit Specifics, and the preliminary progress has orbit calcs. I'd say partial to met. I'll say partial.

Actually the plan does relate to space segment (orbit work before ground control because imaging requirements fix orbit). And preliminary progress applies astrodynamics. I'll say met? It's borderline. I'll say partial because launch/orbit course material application is still planned, not deeply applied.

R3: met — STK selected, accessed via MECH lab licence. STK is allowed.
R4: met — Gantt chart.
R5: met — Table 2 information sources.
R6: met — preliminary technical content (hand calcs, STK scenario).

Technical issues:
- Reference [6] cited for BoM SST products but is NOAA climate change page — citation-content mismatch.
- "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" — simplification; pH drop ~0.1.
- [4] is a Nature news article rather than the primary Asner method paper; objective 2 "to be refined against the method in [4]" relies on a news article.
- Swath/coverage: 60 km swath at 10 m GSD with 6000 pixels — fine, but the claim "reef up to 250 km wide" and needing 5 passes — reasonable.
- Ground track shift 2,700 km "on the same day" — correct but the phrasing "neighbouring ground tracks are 2,700 km apart on the same day" is fine.
- Inclination 97.8° stated without showing the J2 calculation — acceptable.

Overall: strong preliminary report.

Let me write the JSON.

Evidence quotes must be exact contiguous text <=25 words.

C1 evidence: "Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days" — that's 24 words? Let me count: Give(1) reef(2) managers(3) direct,(4) repeatable(5) observations(6) of(7) coral(8) colour(9) over(10) the(11) whole(12) Great(13) Barrier(14) Reef,(15) so(16) that(17) bleaching(18) is(19) detected(20) within(21) days(22) — 22 words. Good.

Also users: "The satellite would be operated by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)." 12 words.

C2 evidence: "Week 10 is float as well as editing time: no new design work is planned in it." 16 words. Or "The order follows the mission: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time" — 20 words.

C3 evidence: "the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes" — 20 words.

C4 evidence: "The document follows a clear and logical structure" — no, that's rubric. Use "Table 2 lists the sources I plan to use and what each is for." 14 words.

Let me finalize.
